facts.statement: Talenkauen lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Talenkauen is a genus of basal iguanodont dinosaur from the Campanian or Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous Cerro Fortaleza Formation

facts.statement: Fossils of Talenkauen have been found in the Austral Basin of Santa Cruz, Argentina.
facts.quote: in the Austral Basin of Santa Cruz, Argentina

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Talenkauen was collected in February 2000 and formally named in 2004 by Fernando E. Novas and colleagues.
facts.quote: the specimen that would become Talenkauen was collected in February 2000 and would later be described and named in a short 2004 paper by Fernando E. Novas and colleagues

facts.statement: Talenkauen was discovered on Los Hornos Hill near the coast of Viedma Lake in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: It was discovered on Los Hornos Hill on the coast of Viedma Lake, in the Santa Cruz Province region of Argentina

facts.statement: An extensive description of Talenkauen was published in 2020 by Sebastián Rozadilla and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2020 an extensive description was published by Sebastián Rozadilla and colleagues

facts.statement: Wear on the 1.7mm wide teeth of a neonatal Talenkauen fossil indicates the baby had hatched and fed shortly before dying.
facts.quote: Wear on the tiny, 1.7mm wide tooth crowns indicate the individual had fed, meaning it was not an embryo and had hatched, but only recently before death

facts.statement: The type specimen of Talenkauen is a partial articulated skeleton missing the rear skull, tail, and hands.
facts.quote: It is based on MPM-10001A, a partial articulated skeleton missing the rear part of the skull, the tail, and the hands

facts.statement: The estimated body length of Talenkauen is no more than 4 meters.
facts.quote: The full length of the body is estimated at no more than 4 m

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Talenkauen to be 4.7 meters long and weigh 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: However, Gregory S. Paul gave a higher estimate of 4.7 m in length and 300 kg in body mass

facts.statement: Talenkauen retained premaxillary teeth at the tip of its beak and a first toe, features lost in more derived iguanodontians.
facts.quote: Unlike more derived iguanodontians, it still had teeth in the tip of the beak (premaxillary teeth), and a first toe

facts.statement: Talenkauen is notable for smooth, ovoid plates located along the sides of its rib cage.
facts.quote: Talenkauen is most noted for a set of smooth, ovoid plates found along the side of the rib cage

facts.statement: The rib plates of Talenkauen could be up to 180 millimeters long but were only 3 millimeters thick.
facts.quote: These plates can be long (180 millimeters, or 7.1 in), but are very thin (only 3 millimeters thick [0.1 in])

facts.statement: Researchers suggested Talenkauen's rib plates might function like uncinate processes found in birds and crocodiles to help ventilate lungs.
facts.quote: Novas and colleagues suggested that the plates may be homologous to uncinate processes, strip-like bony projections found on the ribs of a variety of animals including the tuatara, crocodiles, birds, and some maniraptoran theropod dinosaurs

facts.statement: In 2015, analysis showed that several other Patagonian and Antarctic ornithopods are related to Talenkauen.
facts.quote: In 2015, several other Patagonian and Antarctic ornithopods were also found to be related

facts.statement: As a basal ornithopod, Talenkauen was likely a small, bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Talenkauen, as a basal ornithopod, would have been a small, bipedal herbivore

facts.statement: The most unusual feature of Talenkauen is the presence of small bony plates along the sides of its ribs.
facts.quote: Lo más inusual, es la presencia de pequeñas placas óseas a los lados de las costillas

facts.statement: The same formation as Talenkauen has yielded the giant titanosaur Puertasaurus and the large predator Orkoraptor.
facts.quote: En la misma formación se ha encontrado el enorme Puertasaurus y el gran depredador megarraptoriano Orkoraptor

facts.statement: Unlike more derived iguanodontians, Talenkauen possessed teeth in the premaxillary space where a beak and first toe would typically be located.
facts.quote: A diferencia de los iguanodóntianos más derivados posee dientes en el espacio premaxilar donde estaría el pico y el primer dedo del pie.

facts.statement: The most distinctive feature of Talenkauen was the presence of smooth, oval plates around the rib cage.
facts.quote: La característica más distintiva de Talenkauen son las placas lisas y ovales encontradas alrededor de la caja torácica.

facts.statement: The rib cage plates of Talenkauen measured about 18 millimeters in diameter but were only 3 millimeters thick.
facts.quote: Estas placas medían alrededor de 18 milímetros de diámetro pero solo 3 de espesor, siendo muy delgadas.

facts.statement: Researchers propose that the thin rib plates of Talenkauen functioned in respiratory mechanisms, similar to uncinate processes in birds.
facts.quote: Novas et al. proponen que las placas funcionaron en los mecanismos de respiración de Talenkauen.

facts.statement: Talenkauen was collected in February 2000 and formally described and named in a 2004 article by Fernando E. Novas and colleagues.
facts.quote: El espécimen que se convertiría en Talenkauen se recolectó en febrero de 2000 y luego sería descrito y nombrado en un breve artículo de 2004 por Fernando E. Novas y colegas.

facts.statement: Talenkauen fossils were discovered at Cerro Los Hornos on the shore of Lake Viedma in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en el Cerro Los Hornos en la costa del Lago Viedma, en la Provincia de Santa Cruz región de Argentina.

facts.statement: Talenkauen fossils originate from the Cerro Fortaleza Formation.
facts.quote: Geológicamente, proviene de la Formación Cerro Fortaleza.

facts.statement: The name Talenkauen comes from the Aonikenk language words for 'small' and 'skull', translating to 'small skull'.
facts.quote: El nombre Talenkauen se deriva de las palabras del idioma aonikenk Talenk, que significa pequeño, y kauen, que significa cráneo, por lo que se traduce como "craneo pequeño".

facts.statement: The species name T. santacrucensis refers to the Santa Cruz Province in Argentina where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: El nombre específico T. santacrucensis se refiere a la provincia de Argentina donde se encontró.

facts.statement: A collection of tiny bone and tooth fragments found within the holotype matrix is considered to be a newborn Talenkauen baby associated with an adult.
facts.quote: Se ha reconocido que, anidado entre la matriz de roca del espécimen holotipo, hay una colección de minúsculos fragmentos de huesos y dientes. Identificable como los dientes de algún grado de ornitópodo, y asociado con el espécimen adulto, se considera que es un espécimen de bebé recién nacido de Talenkauen.

facts.statement: Wear on the 1.7-millimeter-wide tooth crowns of the juvenile specimen indicates it had begun feeding, confirming it was a newborn rather than an embryo.
facts.quote: El desgaste de las diminutas coronas dentales de 1,7 milímetros de ancho indica que el individuo se había alimentado, lo que significa que no era un embrión y había nacido solo recientemente antes de morir.

facts.statement: It is possible that the adult Talenkauen practiced parental care because the juvenile was found with an adult, though concrete proof is still needed.
facts.quote: Se señaló como posible que el adulto haya estado practicando el cuidado parental debido a que los individuos se encontraron juntos, pero que se necesitarían pruebas más concretas para hacer tal afirmación con confianza.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses placed Talenkauen in a group more basal than Dryosaurus and Anabisetia, but more derived than Tenontosaurus and Gasparinisaura.
facts.quote: A través de los análisis cladísticos, colocaron al nuevo género en un grupo más basal que Dryosaurus y Anabisetia, pero más derivado que Tenontosaurus y Gasparinisaura.

facts.statement: Researchers who described Macrogryphosaurus later found it related to Talenkauen and created the clade Elasmaria to contain them.
facts.quote: Más recientemente, quienes describieran a Macrogryphosaurus encontraron que este género y Talenkauen estaban relacionados, y acuñaron el clado Elasmaria para contenerlos.

facts.statement: Talenkauen lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Talenkauen belongs to the parent group Elasmaria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Elasmaria

facts.statement: Talenkauen is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
